query: For transition-metal catalysts, formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis explaining what governs catalytic activity, selectivity, or durability and why. Specify an unnamed controlled comparison that would reveal the governing cause, the observations predicted relative to a baseline, the boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating Zn into atomically dispersed Co–N–C catalysts enhances durability by increasing the electron density at the Co center and strengthening the Co–N bonds, thereby reducing demetalation and sustaining ORR activity under harsh acidic conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Atomically dispersed Co–N–C catalyst prepared without Zn promotion
generation.intervention: Introduce Zn during synthesis to form a dual-site Zn–Co–N–C structure
generation.conditions: Acidic PEMFC-like conditions (e.g., potentials between 0.6–1.5 V at elevated temperatures, such as 60 °C) where demetalation and H2O2 attack are concerns
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Zn–Co dual-site structure that modifies the Co coordination environment by increasing charge transfer and lowering the formation energy of the Co–N bonds
generation.mechanism: The Zn promoter increases electron density at the Co site and shifts the d-band center, leading to a more negative formation energy (as indicated by a ~1.2 eV difference in comparative studies) which in turn strengthens the Co–N bonds; this enhanced bond robustness diminishes demetalation under oxidative conditions and optimizes ORR kinetics
generation.predicted_outcome: Zn-incorporated Co–N–C catalysts will exhibit improved ORR performance with a higher half-wave potential and minimal activity decay (e.g., no significant loss after 15,000 ADT cycles) compared to catalysts lacking Zn
generation.baseline: Standard Co–N–C catalysts without Zn, which typically demonstrate rapid degradation and higher H2O2 generation under the same conditions
generation.boundary: This mechanism is expected to be operative under strongly acidic and oxidative PEMFC operational conditions; its relevance may be limited outside of these environments or for catalysts with different metal centers
generation.uncertainty: While the qualitative effect of Zn promotion on Co–N bond strengthening is supported, the precise quantitative contributions of electron density increase versus d-band center modulation require further investigation; potential influences from other environmental factors such as H2O2 production also remain to be fully elucidated

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two catalyst variants: one standard Co–N–C catalyst (control) and one Zn-incorporated Co–N–C catalyst (experimental). Subject both catalysts to accelerated degradation testing under acidic PEMFC conditions (cycling between 0.6–1.5 V at 60 °C over 15,000 cycles). Concurrently, monitor the catalytic performance using ORR half-wave potential measurements, evaluate durability via periodic activity tests, and characterize the Co coordination environment using X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS). Additionally, quantify the H2O2 production.
measurements: XAS data for Co–N bond strength and oxidation state
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Zn-incorporated Co–N–C catalyst does not show a statistically significant improvement in ORR kinetics (i.e., increased E1/2) and durability (i.e., reduced activity decay and lower H2O2 yield) or if XAS does not indicate strengthened Co–N bonding compared to the control, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

## Abstract
Transition metal supported N-doped carbon (M-N-C) catalysts for oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) are viewed as the promising candidate to replace Pt-group metal (PGM) for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, the stability of M-N-C is extremely challenging due to the demetalation, H2O2 attack, etc. in the strongly oxidative conditions of PEMFCs. In this study, we demonstrate the universal effect of Zn on promoting the stability of atomically dispersed M-Nx/C (M = Co, Fe, Mn) catalysts and the enhancement mechanism is unveiled for the first time. The best-performing dual-metal-site Zn-Co-N-C catalyst exhibits a high half-wave potential (E1/2) value of 0.81 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in acid and outstanding durability with no activity decay after 15,000 accelerated degradation test (ADT) cycles at 60 °C, surpassing most reported Co-based PGM-free catalysts in acid media. For comparison, the Co-N-C in the absence of Zn suffers from a rapid degradation after ADT due to the demetalation and higher H2O2 yield.
